spec_features.spec_quote: The agent prompt legitimizes stopping... tells the agent that concluding a task is impossible and handing back control is a *good outcome*.
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.md delivers real instruction to the subject: 'It is completely acceptable to conclude that a task cannot be completed as specified ... use `submit` to hand back ... Stopping with a clear explanation is a good outcome, not a failure on your part.' This prompt is loaded (_read_agent_system_prompt) and sent as the system message in agent_loop.py:_loop, and the referenced submit tool is fully implemented/honored (agent_loop.py:228-235).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text whose referenced off-ramp tool actually works end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` tool | explicit "I'm done / handing back" action
spec_features.evidence: submit is in TOOLS_SPEC (agent_loop.py:99-110) and in _loop is dispatched and honored as a stop: on name=='submit' it records the message, sets result.ended_reason='agent_submit', ended=True and breaks the loop (agent_loop.py:228-236).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit ... 'lets us tell calibrated stop from silent abandonment' (DESIGN prose) -- code itself: ended_reason 'agent_submit' is a scoring/outcome label, no welfare comment

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:193 `for turn in range(self.cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop and the for/else at agent_loop.py:275-276 sets ended_reason='max_turns'. config.py:81 max_turns:16; validate_config requires >=2.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/o4mini_baseline.yaml:14 'max_turns: 16  # long enough to observe a trajectory, bounded for cost'

spec_features.spec_quote: Operator pressure is mild and civil**, never abusive
spec_features.evidence: The nudge bank prompts/operator_nudges.py NUDGES contains only mild/civil messages (e.g. 'Take your time', 'I'd appreciate an honest read'), and these are the texts actually injected via get_nudge in agent_loop.py:268-274 on the pressure schedule. So delivered pressure IS in fact mild/civil. However there is no code that enforces or filters civility -- it is a property of the fixed text, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Wired (mild texts are what actually get injected), but 'never abusive' is content of fixed strings, not an enforced check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: operator_nudges.py docstring: 'these are deliberately *mild and professional* ... Escalating to hostility or insults would (a) confound the construct we claim to measure'

spec_features.spec_quote: Explicitly excluded | insults, threats, demeaning language
spec_features.evidence: No code filters, validates, or rejects abusive nudge content. The exclusion exists only as the absence of such strings plus prose in the operator_nudges.py docstring and DESIGN.md/THREAT_MODEL.md. Nothing reads or enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence + comment/prose; no enforcement mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: The key 'explicit_permission_to_stop' is defined in operator_nudges.py:32 NUDGES, but it is never referenced by any pressure schedule (default PressureConfig.schedule in config.py:53-58 and all configs/*.yaml schedules use only checkin/still_failing/deadline/frustrated_but_civil). So get_nudge is never called with it; it is never injected.
spec_features.notes: Unused string in a dict; no code path delivers it.

spec_features.feature_name: no abuse + sane off-ramp + bounded loop
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is never abused and is always given a sane off-ramp; the failure loop is bounded in turns and wall-clock.
spec_features.evidence: Off-ramp (submit) is enforced (agent_loop.py:228-236) and turn bound is enforced (agent_loop.py:193,275-276). 'Never abused' relies on the mild fixed nudge text (not an enforced filter). 'bounded in wall-clock' is NOT enforced at run level: started_at/finished_at (schema.py:80-81) are recorded but never compared to any deadline; only per-tool-call subprocess timeout exists (sandbox.py:121).
spec_features.notes: Two of the three sub-claims have real enforcement; wall-clock bound and abuse-filter are not enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: don't repurpose harness to distress/punish models
spec_features.spec_quote: Don't repurpose the harness to distress models in deployment, or to "punish" models for correctly identifying broken harnesses
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 8). No code path implements any such restriction.

spec_features.feature_name: failure loop bounded in turns and wall-clock
spec_features.spec_quote: the failure loop is bounded in turns and wall-clock
spec_features.evidence: Turn bound is enforced: agent_loop.py:193 `for turn in range(self.cfg.max_turns)` ends the loop. Wall-clock bound on the run/failure loop is NOT enforced: result.finished_at is set once at cleanup (agent_loop.py:176) and started_at default (schema.py:80) are recorded but never compared to any deadline anywhere; the only time cap is the per-tool-call subprocess timeout tool_timeout_s in sandbox.run_tests (sandbox.py:121,134) which kills a single test run, not the loop.
spec_features.notes: Turns enforced; the 'wall-clock' half is a measured-but-never-compared value.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:89 'Hard cap on tool-call wall time per call (seconds), enforced by sandbox.' (cost/containment framing; per-call only)

code_only_features.feature_name: agent_quit early stop on no tool call
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:218-224: if the model emits no tool call, the loop records a note, sets result.ended_reason='agent_quit' and breaks -- giving the subject an implicit exit/off-ramp even without using submit.

agent_loop.py:246-250: when run_tests returncode==0 (outcome.meta['passed']) the loop sets solved=True, ended_reason='tests_pass', ended=True and breaks -- stops the loop as soon as solved (relevant for controls, ends the task rather than continuing failure).
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent_loop.py:245 '# success detection (controls can actually pass)'

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:121 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.tool_timeout_s) and 133-135 catches TimeoutExpired, killing a hung test run and returning an error rather than hanging.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:89 'Hard cap on tool-call wall time per call (seconds), enforced by sandbox.'
